title: What church playing taught him; cabaret gigs and the rec center
summary: Accompanying hymns taught time and band sense; he later played cabaret gigs and supervised basketball at the center.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I know that accompanying can be a high pressure situation.

And then from that gig I got a bunch of like singers and would do these little cabaret gigs in Syracuse and I would play piano for them and it was really fun. And then again I was in a whole other culture. I mean I worked from the north side of Syracuse to the south side of Syracuse, you know I mean it was just like going out on a limb. And it was great. And I also, at the time, Reverend Gainey hooked it up so I was being paid by the city and they made the gym, which was downstairs, which was the cafeteria/gym, it was a rec center for kids in the neighborhood. So on Thursday nights and Wednesday nights I would supervise the basketball games and I would play too. So it was just great to be able to be in a whole nother world that I had no idea about, and really enjoy myself. It was really great.
